title: Tensoring two finite tower-word comparison squares
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite coefficient extension E, tower base b, a scheme T, level n (exponent n+1), and the prescribed TensorCoordinates tc [def-sp-p1-tensor-derived-coordinates]. For arbitrary level words K,K′,L,L′ [def-sp-p1-level-words], suppose the tower arrow f:K.tower→K′.tower is compared with the finite arrow f′:K.etale→K′.etale, and g:L.tower→L′.tower with g′:L.etale→L′.etale. Then the tensor of f and g is compared, between tensorWord(tc,K,L) and tensorWord(tc,K′,L′), with the ordinary finite derived tensor of f′ and g′. The two endpoint comparisons are invertible. No purity, splitting, exceptional adjunction or concentration is assumed.

source.place: (1), tower paragraph, tensor functoriality of the two finite orientation squares; Levels tensor-word construction

proof.text: Each tensorWord comparison is a composite of the site tensor isomorphism, the given derived realization isomorphism, tensor of its two endpoint comparison arrows and inverse tensorEvaluation. Invertibility follows from the two supplied WordComparisons and preservation of isomorphisms by functors.

For the exact site functor, conjugate leftDerivedTensorComparison by leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory. Its naturality in the first variable follows by pasting naturality of the inverse identification, of the left-derived tensor transformation, of tensoring the identification in the second argument, and of tensoring the identification in the first argument. In the second variable the displayed derived constraint is already an isomorphism of functors, so use its naturality directly. Horizontal composition gives simultaneous naturality. This is the same categorical argument as the proved private comparisonTensor_naturality of SmoothPurityMap, now pasted with the second-variable square.

Apply realization to the site square, paste naturality of tc.derived, tensor of the two input comparison squares, and naturality of inverse tensorEvaluation. Four vertical square pastings and associativity give exactly tensorWord.comparison on each side. This works with unit words, zero arrows, empty schemes and arbitrary dimensions because it is functoriality alone.

theorem tensor_word_comparison {T : Scheme.{u}} (n : ℕ)
    (tc : SpTowerP1.TensorCoordinates l E n b T)
    {K K' L L' : SpTowerP1.LevelWord l E n T}
    {f : K.tower ⟶ K'.tower} {g : L.tower ⟶ L'.tower}
    {f' : K.etale ⟶ K'.etale} {g' : L.etale ⟶ L'.etale}
    (hf : SpTowerP1.WordComparison l E n K K' f f')
    (hg : SpTowerP1.WordComparison l E n L L' g g') :
    SpTowerP1.WordComparison l E n
      (SpTowerP1.tensorWord l E n b tc K L) (SpTowerP1.tensorWord l E n b tc K' L')
      ((SpTowerShriek.tensor l E b T).map (Prod.mkHom f g))
      (((Etale.derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (SpTowerP1.levelRing l E n)) T).map
        f').app L.etale ≫
        ((Etale.derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (SpTowerP1.levelRing l E n)) T).obj
          K'.etale).map g')
